description: Engineering hypothesis patterns used by the telemetry specialist to plan investigations, interpret evidence, identify contradictions, and determine when another domain is required.

patterns.name: Radio link reliability impairment
patterns.description: Radio blocks are being decoded unsuccessfully often enough to impair reliable delivery.
applicable_symptoms: poor application performance despite maintained connectivity

supporting_evidence.pattern: DL BLER is elevated materially during the affected scope
UL BLER is elevated materially during the affected scope
BLER degradation aligns temporally with reported service degradation
supporting_evidence.supports: relationship between radio reliability impairment and service impact

supporting_evidence.pattern: Elevated BLER is accompanied by degraded MCS or signal-quality indicators

contradicting_evidence.pattern: BLER remains consistently low throughout the affected period
contradicting_evidence.contradicts: radio reliability impairment as the dominant measured impairment

investigation_sequence: Determine whether impairment is DL, UL, or bidirectional
Assess BLER magnitude, distribution, persistence, and peaks
Check temporal alignment with reported degradation
Inspect signal quality and signal strength
Inspect MCS behavior for link-adaptation response
Inspect resource utilization to separate reliability impairment from congestion
can_conclude: whether impairment is predominantly uplink or downlink
whether available telemetry supports association with service degradation

cross_domain_escalation.when: telemetry supports reliability impairment but the physical or equipment mechanism remains unexplained
cross_domain_escalation.question: Are there radio, hardware, transport, or processing alarms temporally aligned with the impairment?

cross_domain_escalation.when: the impairment may be associated with shared infrastructure or a specific network element
cross_domain_escalation.question: Do affected entities share a common radio or transport dependency?

patterns.name: Coverage degradation
patterns.description: Insufficient received signal strength contributes materially to degraded radio performance.

supporting_evidence.pattern: RSRP is degraded during the affected period
RSRP deterioration aligns with increased BLER
RSRP deterioration aligns with reduced MCS
supporting_evidence.supports: link adaptation responding to poorer radio conditions

supporting_evidence.pattern: Poor RSRP persists across a substantial portion of the affected scope
supporting_evidence.supports: persistent coverage weakness rather than isolated sample variation

contradicting_evidence.pattern: RSRP is strong and stable throughout the degradation
contradicting_evidence.contradicts: weak received signal strength as the primary explanation

investigation_sequence: Inspect RSRP level and distribution
Determine whether poor RSRP is persistent or isolated
Compare RSRP behavior with BLER
Compare RSRP behavior with MCS
Inspect available signal-quality indicators
can_conclude: whether available telemetry supports weak received signal strength
whether signal-strength degradation aligns with measured radio impairment

cross_domain_escalation.when: coverage degradation appears localized to particular network infrastructure
cross_domain_escalation.question: What serving radio elements and shared dependencies are associated with the affected scope?

cross_domain_escalation.when: persistent abnormal signal behavior raises a possible equipment or site issue
cross_domain_escalation.question: Are there radio-unit, antenna-path, site, or related alarms aligned with the degradation?

patterns.name: Signal quality degradation
patterns.description: Radio signal quality is degraded even when received signal strength may remain acceptable.

supporting_evidence.pattern: UL SNR is degraded while UL BLER is elevated
UL SNR deterioration aligns with lower UL MCS
supporting_evidence.supports: link adaptation responding to poorer uplink quality

supporting_evidence.pattern: RSRP remains relatively healthy while SNR and reliability degrade
supporting_evidence.supports: quality impairment not explained by received signal strength alone

contradicting_evidence.pattern: Available signal-quality indicators remain stable and healthy during degradation

investigation_sequence: Inspect available signal-quality metrics
Compare signal quality with BLER
Compare signal quality with MCS
Compare signal quality with signal strength
Determine whether degradation is directional
can_conclude: whether measured signal quality is degraded
whether signal-quality degradation aligns with reliability or link-adaptation changes
data_limitations: Current dataset contains UL_SNR but no explicit DL signal-quality metric such as DL SINR/RSRQ
Current dataset contains no direct interference-power measurement

cross_domain_escalation.when: quality degradation remains unexplained by available telemetry
cross_domain_escalation.question: Are there radio or hardware events aligned with the quality degradation?

patterns.name: Radio resource congestion
patterns.description: Available radio resources are heavily utilized such that demand may exceed or approach available scheduling capacity.

supporting_evidence.pattern: Absolute PRB utilization is persistently high during degradation
High PRB utilization aligns temporally with degraded service behavior
Elevated resource utilization is accompanied by traffic demand or buffer pressure

contradicting_evidence.pattern: Absolute PRB utilization remains consistently low during degradation
contradicting_evidence.contradicts: radio resource saturation as the primary mechanism

contradicting_evidence.pattern: Resource utilization does not increase during degraded periods

investigation_sequence: Inspect absolute DL and UL PRB utilization
Determine whether utilization is persistent or transient
Compare utilization with reported degradation
Inspect traffic demand and packet volume
Inspect estimated UL buffer where directionally relevant
can_conclude: whether radio resource pressure is present
whether available evidence supports or contradicts radio resource congestion

cross_domain_escalation.when: service degradation persists without radio resource saturation and a shared upstream bottleneck is plausible
cross_domain_escalation.question: Do affected entities share a transport or infrastructure dependency?

cross_domain_escalation.when: resource behavior appears abnormal rather than demand-driven
cross_domain_escalation.question: Are scheduler, processing, capacity, or related alarms present?

patterns.name: Link adaptation degradation
patterns.description: MCS behavior indicates adaptation toward less efficient modulation/coding or an abnormal relationship between selected MCS and observed reliability.

supporting_evidence.pattern: MCS decreases during degraded radio conditions
High BLER persists despite MCS adaptation
MCS changes align temporally with reliability degradation
supporting_evidence.supports: relationship between link adaptation and observed impairment

contradicting_evidence.pattern: MCS remains stable while the investigated impairment changes materially
contradicting_evidence.contradicts: MCS behavior as the dominant measured differentiator

investigation_sequence: Inspect DL and UL MCS independently
Compare MCS with corresponding BLER
Compare UL MCS with UL SNR
Compare MCS with RSRP where relevant
Assess temporal alignment rather than averages alone
can_conclude: whether link-adaptation behavior changes during degradation
whether MCS behavior aligns with reliability or signal-quality changes

cross_domain_escalation.when: link-adaptation behavior appears abnormal and an equipment/software mechanism is suspected
cross_domain_escalation.question: Are there relevant radio, scheduler, processing, or software alarms/events?

patterns.name: Uplink-dominant impairment
patterns.description: Measured degradation is materially stronger on the uplink than on the downlink.

supporting_evidence.pattern: UL BLER is materially more impaired than DL BLER
UL SNR degradation aligns with UL BLER or UL MCS degradation
UL resource pressure aligns with reported uplink degradation

contradicting_evidence.pattern: UL metrics remain healthy while DL metrics show dominant degradation

investigation_sequence: Compare UL and DL reliability
Inspect UL SNR
Inspect UL MCS
Inspect UL resource utilization
Inspect UL buffer and traffic indicators
Determine whether impairment is truly directional

patterns.name: Downlink-dominant impairment
patterns.description: Measured degradation is materially stronger on the downlink than on the uplink.

supporting_evidence.pattern: DL BLER is materially more impaired than UL BLER
DL MCS degradation aligns with elevated DL BLER
DL resource pressure aligns with reported downlink degradation

contradicting_evidence.pattern: DL metrics remain healthy while UL metrics show dominant degradation

investigation_sequence: Compare DL and UL reliability
Inspect DL MCS
Inspect DL resource utilization
Inspect DL traffic indicators
Inspect RSRP
Determine whether impairment is truly directional
data_limitations: Current dataset has no direct downlink SINR/SNR metric

patterns.name: Temporal or bursty impairment
patterns.description: The impairment occurs intermittently or in short periods rather than remaining continuously degraded.

supporting_evidence.pattern: Metric degradation appears in repeated time-localized periods separated by recovery
BLER, SNR, MCS, resource, or traffic changes align within the same degraded periods
supporting_evidence.supports: candidate mechanism associated with intermittent behavior

contradicting_evidence.pattern: The relevant metric remains continuously degraded with no meaningful recovery

investigation_sequence: Use event timestamps or sample order
Identify degraded periods
Measure frequency and duration of degradation
Compare candidate metrics within degraded versus recovered periods
Avoid inferring intermittency from average/min/max summaries
can_conclude: whether measured impairment is intermittent or persistent
which measured variables align with degraded periods

cross_domain_escalation.when: periodic telemetry degradation may align with repeated operational events
cross_domain_escalation.question: Do alarm activation/clear cycles align with the degraded periods?

patterns.name: Uplink buffer or queue pressure
patterns.description: Uplink demand accumulates in the available buffer indicator, potentially contributing to delayed or constrained uplink delivery.

supporting_evidence.pattern: Estimated UL buffer increases during affected periods
Buffer growth aligns with elevated UL resource utilization
Buffer growth aligns with reported uplink degradation
supporting_evidence.supports: association between backlog and service impact

contradicting_evidence.pattern: Estimated UL buffer remains consistently low during uplink degradation
contradicting_evidence.contradicts: buffer pressure as the dominant measured mechanism

investigation_sequence: Inspect Estimated_UL_Buffer behavior
Compare buffer behavior with UL PRB utilization
Compare with UL packet and byte activity
Compare with UL BLER and UL MCS
Assess temporal alignment with degradation
can_conclude: whether the available buffer indicator shows uplink pressure

patterns.name: Mobility-associated degradation
patterns.description: Measured degradation is associated with mobility context or changing radio conditions, without assuming a handover failure.

supporting_evidence.pattern: The affected window is associated with mobility and radio metrics vary materially over time
Signal/reliability/link-adaptation degradation aligns with changing radio conditions

contradicting_evidence.pattern: The window is stationary and relevant radio metrics remain stable

investigation_sequence: Inspect mobility metadata
Inspect temporal RSRP behavior
Inspect BLER and MCS behavior
Inspect available signal-quality behavior
Determine whether the current dataset contains enough evidence to investigate handover mechanisms
can_conclude: whether degradation is associated with mobility context and changing telemetry
data_limitations: Current telemetry schema contains mobility context but no explicit handover event/counter fields

cross_domain_escalation.when: handover or mobility failure is suspected but telemetry lacks event-level evidence
cross_domain_escalation.question: Are there mobility, handover, radio-link, or related events during the affected period?
What serving and neighboring network relationships are relevant to the affected entity?
